name: NORWAY

flag.title: The Norwegian Flag
flag.note: Red with a blue cross edged in white

lead: Norway perches at the top of Europe where mountains plunge into sea-inlets called fjords. In summer the sun never sets for weeks. In winter, green ribbons called the Northern Lights dance overhead. Vikings sailed from here a thousand years ago. Today Norwegians are famous for skiing, trolls, and the world's biggest national piggy bank.

geo: Norway stretches 1,752 km from south to north — incredibly long and narrow. Glaciers carved thousands of deep fjords into the coastline, creating inlets where ships sail between walls of rock rising 1,400 m straight up from emerald water.

Over 50,000 islands fringe the coast and 150,000 lakes dot the land. In the far north, the sun stays up 76 days in a row in summer. The world's longest road tunnel, Lærdalstunnellen, bores 24.5 km through the mountains.
animals: Norway's unofficial national animal is the moose — the biggest creature in its forests, weighing as much as a small car. Reindeer roam wild in the uplands, and wolves, bears, and lynx still prowl the dark forests.

Coastal waters hold puffins, seals, and humpback whales. In the Arctic north lives the fluffy Arctic fox, whose thick coat keeps it warm down to −70 °C. Trolls are mythical only — but Norwegians love them very much.
culture: Every 17 May, Constitution Day turns the country into one giant children's parade. Bands march, flags wave, and everyone eats hot dogs and ice cream. Many Norwegians wear a bunad — a hand-embroidered costume whose colours show exactly which valley their family is from.

Skiing was invented here some 4,000 years ago — rock carvings prove it. Today cross-country skiing is practically a national religion. Norwegians also leave babies to nap outside in prams in winter, trusting that cold fresh air builds strong children.
history: Vikings launched from Norway's fjords over 1,000 years ago, reaching Iceland, Greenland, and North America long before Columbus. Expert sailors and traders, they crossed oceans in dragon-prowed longships that are still iconic today.

Oil was found on Christmas Eve 1969, transforming a small fishing nation. Norway saved most of the money. By 2026 its oil fund topped $2 trillion — over $350,000 per citizen — making it the world's largest sovereign wealth fund.
wows: Norway has over 50,000 islands — so many that no one has settled on an exact count.
The Norwegian paperclip, patented in 1900, became a WWII symbol of national resistance.
Norway's oil fund owns roughly 1.5% of every listed company on Earth.
The Lærdal Tunnel at 24.5 km is the world's longest road tunnel for cars.
In Svalbard it is against the rules to die — the permafrost cannot accommodate graves.
Norway gifts Finland a Christmas tree each year as thanks for WWII solidarity.
Galdhøpiggen is Northern Europe's highest peak and 30,000 people climb it yearly.

myths.fact: The Gulf Stream keeps Bergen's winters mild and Tromsø, inside the Arctic Circle, often sits above freezing. Coastal Norway is warmer than its latitude suggests.

myths.myth: Northern Lights appear every clear night
myths.fact: The aurora needs strong solar activity and full darkness. In Oslo, some residents live their whole lives without ever seeing the lights.
